type: For any variable type σ with Fintype σ and d,k:σ→₀ℕ, hasseCoeff d k = ∏j, Nat.choose (k j) (d j). No coefficient type R or semiring assumption occurs in the actual type.
what: Replaces the support product of coordinatewise binomial coefficients by the full product over finite variables.
how: Specializes Finsupp.prod_fintype with the unit condition Nat.choose_zero_right; exactly two mathlib calls.
hypotheses: Arbitrary universe-polymorphic variable type, finite enumeration and two natural multiindices. No dominance, field, characteristic, nontriviality, nonempty or coefficient-ring assumption.
caller_summary: One explicit same-file caller: MvPolynomial.hasseCoeff_le_two_pow at Roth/HasseDeriv.lean:276, invocation 278. Zero callers outside the declaring file. No identical inline duplicate; nearby support-subset binomial and full power-product uses are related generic routes. Explicit source audit only.
mathlib_api_audit: All five methods searched concrete/literature and abstract forms. Finsupp.prod_fintype (BigOperators/Finsupp/Basic:63) plus Nat.choose_zero_right (Choose/Basic:56) proves the exact target. Isolated pinned check and complete caller rewrite verified; unavailable local index supplies no absence evidence.
moral_duplications: A specialization of generic identity-padding of a finitely supported product. Multinomial factorial ratios are a false friend, not the same coefficient.
generalization: Verified expanded version accepts arbitrary upper k:σ→ℕ with the same proof. Generic factor/CommMonoid and finite ambient-set forms already exist in mathlib. The literal full ∏j expression needs Fintype; upper-function widening needs no new product construction.
missing_api: None for the support/full-product bridge: Finsupp.prod_fintype and prod_of_support_subset already cover it.
junk: Useful local semantic rewrite with one caller, but a redundant standalone upstream wrapper; not narrow rfl/unfold glue.
action: NO-composable-from-mathlib: inline d.prod_fintype _ (fun _ ↦ Nat.choose_zero_right _) at the sole bound caller and delete the wrapper in a future source refactor. Retaining it in the project-local Hasse package remains possible while the alias is kept; no standalone mathlib addition is needed.
